doc.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

title: Justifying ear training in academia
summary: Rowe asks about defending listening courses; Blake credits Gunther Schuller and colleagues for support.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you have times in academia where it was a bit difficult to justify spending so much time on developing an ear. I guess what I’m trying to say is you have to justify courses to an academic council.
And to say we’re going to spend a whole semester listening.

Yeah, and you’ll perform ten — thank gosh I’ve had Gunther Schuller to start me off, Hankus and Eden MacAdams, who’ve really have supported me. These are faculty and through the years I’ve had some students really very interested, impressed, maybe exalted that they can do this, but it does take time. Big bands expect you to read well and of course they should, and some of my students were from, were orchestra players doing music from the Baroque to the modern. So they may feel some kind of a cult.
